title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 21
statement: In the given figure hexagon \(ABCDEF\) is equiangular, \(ABJI\) and \(FEHG\) are squares with areas \(18\) and \(32\) respectively, \(\triangle JBK\) is equilateral and \(FE=BC.\) What is the area of \(\triangle KBC?\)

solutions.text:
The square with area \(18\) has side length \(JB=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2.\) Since \(\triangle JBK\) is equilateral, \(BK=3\sqrt2.\)

The square with area \(32\) has side length \(FE=\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt2.\) Since \(FE=BC,\) we have \(BC=4\sqrt2.\)

At \(B,\) the equilateral triangle, square, and equiangular hexagon contribute angles of \(60^\circ,\) \(90^\circ,\) and \(120^\circ,\) respectively. Hence \[\begin{aligned} \angle KBC &= 360^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\\ &\qquad-120^\circ\\ &=90^\circ. \end{aligned}\] Therefore \[[\triangle KBC]=\dfrac12(3\sqrt2)(4\sqrt2)=12.\]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Find \(JB\) and \(BC\) from the two square areas.
In the diagram, \(BK\) is perpendicular to \(BC.\)
